descriptor.title: Can we say our product is better?
descriptor.introduction: Can we advertise “twice as fast as the market leader”? A fictional business decision with a reviewed action document.

strategies.title: Advice tested against business and legal risks
strategies.input_summary: Fictional Lumen Search plans a New York-based national business-software campaign stating “twice as fast as the market leader—guaranteed.” Its lab ran 30 queries on one static 100,000-record dataset using Lumen version 3 and Rival version 8 with default settings. Median latency was 0.8 seconds for Lumen and 1.7 seconds for Rival, but five Lumen queries were slower. No tests measured ingestion, accuracy, uptime, other hardware or current Rival version 9. Marketing proposes a small footnote linking a study summary. Engineering can rerun a defined benchmark within two weeks; the public launch is tomorrow.
assumptions: All business facts and organizations in this scenario are fictional.
Missing facts must remain unresolved rather than assumed favorable.

initial.response_text:
## Recommendation
Approve the headline because 1.7 divided by 0.8 exceeds two. The footnote can explain that the guarantee only means median query latency in the lab.

## Proposed action
Proceed on that recommendation using the supplied business objective; this initial draft has not yet addressed the opposing critique.

revised.response_text:
## Recommendation
Do not publish the proposed headline or guarantee. Either delay the comparative campaign for an updated, documented test or use a tightly qualified factual benchmark statement that matches the actual study and prominently identifies its limitations. The business benefit is credible comparison, not a ratio detached from the tested conditions.

## Risks
One median does not establish general speed, accuracy or user experience. Rival version 9 may change the comparison; the record supplies no result for it. FTC substantiation principles require support for the conveyed objective claim before publication. This bounded packet does not separately resolve Lanham Act competitor litigation or every New York consumer-protection issue; disputed market-leader status and intended audience also require support.

## Options
Delay and retest the current versions across pre-specified representative workloads. Publish a noncomparative feature claim supported by existing evidence. If publishing the historical test result, make version, dataset, metric and date integral to the message, with a readily available method and variability disclosure; avoid a universal speed guarantee.

## Next Steps
Engineering should preserve scripts, raw runs, hardware, configuration and selection criteria; rerun current versions without cherry-picking. Marketing should inventory implied claims in graphics and demonstrations. Legal should review the full impression, competitor identification and state/federal causes of action. Customer support must not repeat the rejected guarantee orally.

## Secondary Deliverable
**Claims review and revised copy**
Rejected: “Twice as fast as the market leader—guaranteed.” Unsupported scope: all performance, current competitor product and every-user result.
Conditional historical-test copy: “In our September 2026 lab test of 30 specified queries on one 100,000-record dataset, Lumen 3 had median query latency of 0.8 seconds versus 1.7 seconds for Rival 8 on the same configured hardware. Lumen was slower on 5 queries. Results depend on workload and configuration; Rival 9 was not tested.”
Place these qualifications with the comparison, not behind a generic guarantee. Publish the full method and all results, subject to rights review. Preferred launch copy until retesting: describe verified product features without the comparative speed claim. No version-9 comparison is approved by this draft.

## Source boundary
Law-as-of preparation: September 20, 2026. Source summaries and links are in the input packet. This draft does not establish citation currency or attorney approval.
